r0-context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-crew.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas if present: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, plus the handoff, the diff, and the relevant packet. r0-context.finding: Loaded global-crew.md, global-everyone.md, docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, the g1-review handoff, g1-target-content.md, g1-implement-result.md; confirmed git status/diff scope matches the 4 named files.

r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: Change matches g1-target-content.md byte-for-byte (verified programmatically) and all 5 Close Criteria pass. BUT the handoff's own Constraints section names '## MCP door and ## Session lease sections of checklist-engine.md especially' as needing to be byte-identical to the pre-change file, and Stop Conditions says BLOCK if 'any retained section is not byte-identical to the original.' Empirically diffed pre-change (git show HEAD:...) vs post-change checklist-engine.md: '## MCP door' section IS byte-identical (confirmed, matches Stop Conditions explicit check). '## Session lease' section is NOT byte-identical: shrank from 5 bullets (2255 chars) to 2 bullets (1336 chars) -- the heartbeat bullet and the 'every mutating verb needs --session-id' bullet were deleted outright, and the surviving 'stale' bullet was itself reworded/shortened (dropped the self-heal clause and the 'engine refuses it and tells it to claim' clause). tests/test_mcp_adoption.py's test_lease_section_carries_door_equivalent only checks substring presence of claim/heartbeat/release/spine_lease -- it does not pin exact text there, so tests stay green despite the rewording. Root cause: g1-target-content.md itself (the authoritative full-replacement spec the implementer correctly applied verbatim) already contains this shortened Session-lease text -- this is a plan-level inconsistency between the target-content spec and the handoff's own stated byte-identical constraint, not an implementer deviation.

r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect specific exclusions? Record pass/fail with a finding.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Independently reproduced (not just re-read) every claimed piece of evidence: (1) foreground pytest run of the 3 named test files POST-change: 388 passed, 2 skipped, 506 subtests, matches claim exactly; (2) stashed the 4-file diff and re-ran the SAME suite PRE-change: also 388 passed, 2 skipped, 506 subtests, then restored the stash and confirmed git status/diff returned to the pre-stash state -- baseline claim independently reproduced from scratch, not trusted; (3) programmatic byte-exact comparison of the 3 full-replacement files against g1-target-content.md's extracted blocks: all 3 match; (4) grep -c sentinel count is exactly 1; (5) git diff --name-only shows exactly the 4 allowed files. All required evidence is present and actually demonstrates the claimed behavior.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Checked both named constraints individually. (1) 'No template under skills/workbench/templates/ moved, renamed, or edited' -- PASS, git diff --stat on that path is empty. (2) 'The retained prose (## MCP door and ## Session lease sections of checklist-engine.md especially) must be byte-identical to the pre-change file' -- PARTIAL: MCP door section is confirmed byte-identical (git show HEAD vs working tree, exact string equality); Session lease section is NOT byte-identical -- see r1-handoff finding for the full diff (5 bullets -> 2 bullets, wording changed even in survivors). This is the same underlying issue as r1-handoff, recorded again here because this item is specifically 'quality vs the handoff's named constraints' and constraint (2) is directly violated for one of its two named sections.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: Both named decision anchors from the handoff's Map Anchors are honored: 'workbench stays a template package' (templates/ untouched, skill still ships templates/), and 'partial not full deletion, settle: full suite green post-change' (settled -- full suite reproduced green both pre- and post-change). No docs/architecture/ map exists in this repo to check for a separate structural-drift signal. However, the r1-handoff/r4-quality finding IS a reconciliation item Commander must resolve: g1-target-content.md's checklist-engine.md block does not preserve the '## Session lease' section byte-identical, contradicting the handoff's own stated constraint for that section. Commander must decide: (a) amend target-content.md to restore the 5 original Session-lease bullets verbatim and re-run g1-implement, or (b) explicitly relax/correct the 'byte-identical ... especially Session lease' constraint text as no-longer-applicable now that the plan deliberately shrinks that section too (only its claim/heartbeat/release/spine_lease substance is test-pinned, not its exact wording). This is in-scope for g1, not an out-of-scope triage candidate.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards -- an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to .agent-work/<work-id>/FOWLER_PASS.json (from templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/<work-id>/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. Do NOT silently skip this item.
